info.title: tonearm
info.description: Unofficial personal Apple Music API — powered by your own logged-in web player session. Not affiliated with Apple.

get.description:
Every track of a library playlist (auto-paginated to the end).
NOTE: declared before the generic routes so it wins the match.

Full library dump as JSON — every song + every playlist (with track
ids). Slow by design: walks the entire library (~100 s per 9k songs).
Point a cron at this for backups; the output is a complete restore
reference (ids) if the library is ever lost.

What changed in your library since a unix timestamp.

Apple has no "changed since" filter — this diff is OURS, computed from
the local store's watermark columns (first_seen / last_seen /
last_changed) across snapshot walks. So:
  * `since=0` (default) -> the whole library as `added`
  * removals become visible on the FIRST walk AFTER they happen
  * `what` filters: added | updated | removed | all

schema.title: Response Library Diff Api Library Diff Get

get.description: Search YOUR library across songs/albums/artists/playlists.

schema.title: Response Library Search Api Library Search Get

get.description:
Most recently added library items (any kind).
Apple caps this endpoint's limit at 25 — asked for 100 it 400s
(found live from the Radar page).
List any library resource, fully paginated by the caller.
One library item, with its relationships (e.g. an album's track list).
A relationship collection, e.g. /library/albums/{id}/tracks.

Multi-type catalog search. `types` is a comma list, e.g.
songs,albums,artists,playlists,stations,curators,music-videos

schema.title: Response Catalog Search Api Catalog Search Get

get.description:
Search suggestions (what the web player's autocomplete shows).
Returns flat rows: {term/title, id, kind}.

Synced lyrics for a catalog song (Apple's TTML, parsed to lines).
`raw=1` returns the raw TTML document. Songs without lyrics -> 404.
Catalog charts: most-played songs/albums/playlists. `genre` = genre id.

schema.title: Response Charts Api Catalog Charts Get

get.description: Fetch specific catalog resources by (comma-separated) id.
One catalog item; `extend=tracks` etc. includes relationships inline.
e.g. /catalog/artists/{id}/albums, /catalog/albums/{id}/tracks.
'Listen Now' / For You recommendations (albums & playlists, grouped).
Albums and playlists you've had in heavy rotation.
Your recently played items (Apple caps this at 20).
Apple's auto-generated personal playlists (Favorites Mix, New Music…).

Every song in your Favorite Songs playlist (auto-paginated, with art).
Also returns `playlist_id` so clients can browse it like any playlist.
Apple's favorites auto-sync lags ~60s+; `?fresh=1` bypasses the read
cache when you need the live state.

The current queue (also pushed by the SSE stream — prefer the
stream; this is the one-shot read).

put.description:
Reorder the queue: send the FULL ordered list of item ids (#87 —
whole-list PUT semantics, last write wins, no deltas). The playhead
stays on the same track at its new index. Best-effort like every
transport op: MusicKit has no public reorder, so the queue is rebuilt
and the playhead is moved back onto the same track.

get.description: shuffle / repeat / volume / playing state in one shot.

post.description: Start playing a catalog song by id (clears the queue).

Queue a whole album/playlist/station and play it.
kind: album | playlist | station  (catalog ids)
Insert a catalog song to play next.
Append a catalog song to play later.

Hardware-button 'back' (the Tidbyt's triple-tap): past the
threshold (default 10s), 'back' means RESTART this song; before it,
previous track. Additive route, not a change to /previous — the
freeze's allowlist is additions only.
play | pause | toggle | next | previous.
Favorite (heart) a song. `library_key=true` for library-keyed tracks.

delete.description:
Unfavorite a song. Verify with GET /api/favorites — a wrong-key delete
returns success without doing anything.

get.description:
Current rating of a song: null = none, 1 = like.
Ratings lag server-side after a mutation; `?fresh=1` bypasses cache.

post.description:
Add catalog songs to your library. Body is a bare JSON array of
catalog song ids. NOTE: 202-accepted (async on Apple's side); the
songs appear in the library a moment later.

delete.description:
Remove a song from your library by its library id (i.XXX).
This is NOT the same as unfavoriting. Destructive — no undo.

post.description:
Add catalog albums (all their tracks) to your library.
Body: bare JSON array of catalog album ids. 202-async.

delete.description:
Remove a whole library album (l.XXX) — all its songs go too.
Destructive — no undo.

post.description: Create a library playlist. Returns the new playlist id.

Append catalog songs to a playlist (auto-adds them to the library).
Body is a bare JSON array of catalog song ids.

put.description:
REPLACE the track list, in order. Body is a bare JSON array of
library-songs ids. This is both reorder and removal: send the full
list minus any song you want gone.
e.g.  curl -X PUT -d '["i.abc","i.def"]' /api/write/playlists/{pid}/tracks

delete.description: Delete a library playlist. Destructive — no undo.

post.description:
Restore playlists from a /api/library/export JSON body.

DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT: returns the plan (per playlist: exists/create,
per track: catalog-id / name-match / unmatched-with-reason).
`?execute=1` runs it: creates missing playlists, adds tracks, verifies
counts with bounded retries (Apple's applies are async).

The unmatched report is the contract: nothing is ever dropped silently.

schema.title: Response Restore Api Write Restore Post

get.description: Dry-run: groups of duplicate library rows. Nothing is touched.

post.description:
Remove all-but-first row of each duplicate group.
Pass ?execute=1 to actually run it.

schema.title: Response Dedupe Execute Api Write Sweeps Dedupe Post

get.description:
Dry-run: which library songs a batch-rate would heart.
(Execution re-checks each song's current rating and skips hearts.)

post.description:
Heart every library song matching the filter, skipping songs that
already have a rating. Pass ?execute=1 to actually run it.

schema.title: Response Rate Execute Api Write Sweeps Rate Post

get.description:
Read-only report: library songs with no reported plays.
NOTE: Apple's API currently does not expose play counts on
library-songs at all — when that's the case this reports
`play_count_available: false` rather than pretending every song is
unplayed.

Dry-run digest: dedupe + never-played from ONE library walk.
The same payload is emitted as `sweep.digest` on the scheduled cadence
(TONEARM_DIGEST_INTERVAL + TONEARM_WEBHOOKS=1).

Live mp3 of whatever the server's Apple Music session is playing.
Point an <audio> element at it. ~1-2 s behind the reported playhead —
X-Tonearm-Join-* headers describe the alignment at subscribe time.
Live Ogg Vorbis of the session's audio (same capture as mp3).
Live Opus (in Ogg) of the session's audio — smallest bandwidth.

Raw signed 16-bit little-endian stereo PCM at 44.1kHz for the
Tidbyt's Bluetooth A2DP source prototype. No codec or TLS is needed on
the device; the plain relay carries only this scoped-key stream.

Prometheus text format. Carries no user data, but sits behind
TONEARM_API_KEY when one is set (scrape config: `authorization` block with
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`).

Everything you've played since TONEARM_STORE=1 was first enabled,
newest first. No backfill: Apple only ever exposed ~20 recent items,
so coverage starts when the store turns on.

Top artists / tracks from the LOCAL play archive (not Apple's).
window: day | week | month | all. Plays dedupe on (track_id, started_at)
is the writer's guarantee, so counts are play-starts.
Plays per day, last N days — bucketed in SQL, ready for a chart.
Now-playing as JSON — for OBS browser sources and bots.

Now-playing as one text line. `?format=` is a template with
{title} {artist} {album} {elapsed} {duration} placeholders — unknown
fields and missing values render as ''. Text (not JSON) on purpose:
OBS's classic Text source wants a plain line.

Configured hooks (secrets redacted), pending deliveries and the last
few attempts. Delivery is at-least-once; consumers dedupe on event `id`.

post.description:
Add a webhook. `events` is an optional filter (empty = everything);
`secret` enables HMAC-SHA256 signing. Adding an existing URL updates it.

get.description: The last N delivery attempts (newest first), retries included.

patch.description:
Partial update. Omitted fields stay as they are; `secret: ""` clears
the signing secret.

delete.description: Remove a hook. Already-queued deliveries for it still go out.

post.description:
Deliver a `webhook.test` event right now and report the result.
No background retry — this is a diagnostic, not an event.

get.description: All smart-playlist definitions with their last evaluation/sync state.

post.description:
Define a smart playlist. Rules are validated eagerly — a bad rule is
a 400 here, never a silent empty list later.

patch.description:
Partial update. Replaces whichever fields are present; rules are
re-validated in full whenever they appear.

get.description: The evaluation, served from the store — no Apple calls at all.

post.description:
Evaluate + materialize: find-or-create the live playlist, then one
full-list PUT so Apple matches the evaluation exactly. Requires
TONEARM_ENABLE_WRITES=1 (evaluation-only? use /preview).

get.description:
Watcher state. Artists that have never resolved to a catalog id are
reported honestly (`mapped` vs `watched`) — a bad mapping is data, not
a silent zero.

post.description:
One bounded pass, synchronously. Same code the scheduler runs —
useful for the live verification (and for cron'ing it yourself).

get.description:
Stream a firmware file to the page. The page origin (:8443) differs
from the funnel file host (:10000), and the file server sends no CORS
headers, so the page fetches through here. Host allowlisted.

Stream a firmware file to the page. The page origin (:8443) differs
from the funnel file host (:10000), and the file server sends no CORS
headers, so the page fetches through here. Host allowlisted.

post.description:
N reads, one round trip. Every entry is answered as its own
envelope: {status, body} (4xx/5xx per-entry — one bad request never
sinks the batch).

Accept only a short, allowlisted session summary; never accept
prompts, code, tool arguments, or arbitrary event payloads.

BatchEntry.title: BatchEntry
BatchEntry.description:
One inner result: {status, body} — body is whatever the inner
route would have answered (error envelope on 4xx/5xx).

DiffAll.title: DiffAll
DiffAll.description: `what=all` (the default): all three pages + the last walk cursor.

ItemRow.title: ItemRow
ItemRow.description:
mk.item_row — any resource: song fields + kind + the RAW attributes
blob (every field Apple exposes, unfiltered).

OverlayNowPlaying.title: OverlayNowPlaying
OverlayNowPlaying.description:
OBS overlay payload — NowPlaying + the playing item's id (what the
SSE `update` events carry), so overlays can also resolve lyrics/art.

QueueReorder.title: QueueReorder
QueueReorder.description:
PUT /api/playback/queue body — the FULL ordered list of queue item
ids (#87: whole-list PUT, never deltas). The playhead stays on the same
track at its new index.

SessionState.title: SessionState
SessionState.description: The Apple session, as far as tonearm's own calls can tell (#189).

SmartlistPreview.title: SmartlistPreview
SmartlistPreview.description: The local evaluation — store rows only, no Apple touched.

WatcherArtist.title: WatcherArtist
WatcherArtist.description: One row of watcher state: the mapping cache + newest release seen.

apiKeyQuery.name: api_key
apiKeyQuery.description: ?api_key=<TONEARM_API_KEY> — the fallback EventSource needs (it cannot send headers)
